headline: A UK cybersecurity research network has apologised and will re-review every grant proposal its AI screen rejected, after academics complained that no human read them.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a funder reversal over AI screening of grant proposals, but limited to one pilot call of 179 proposals.
importance_line: Researchers whose proposals were screened out get a human review, and CRANE itself admits it was not transparent enough about using AI, but no date for the new decisions has been given and the apology covers one pilot call.
summary: Times Higher Education reports that CRANE, a UK cybersecurity research network supported by the national funder UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), has apologised for not being transparent enough about its AI screening of grant proposals and will have every screened-out proposal reviewed again and reconvene its funding panel, with offers already made suspended. This answers the outcry that followed Times Higher Education's own report of 27 Sep 2026 that an AI screen using several models had rejected about half of the 179 proposals in the pilot call before any human read them.
notes: Read in full, plus THE's first report of 27 Sep 2026 (read in full). The pool marks this as a follow-up of Science's 4 Oct 2026 story 'U.K. funder uses AI triage to reject grant proposals' (headline only seen); no edition of ours carried either story. CRANE's apology is quoted from a letter THE saw; no second source for it, and THE says CRANE and UKRI were approached for comment.
